answers.finding: The instruction asked to keep fewer stored height fields per step so each loop takes much less than 1 GB. The session dropped all height-field arrays from fields.npz for the width-200 passes (D0054), keeping only the Fourier spectrum and variance (121 KB per step compressed versus 2465 KB for the height grid). Per loop: about 390 MB, down from about 880 MB. The queue spec carries SEQUEL_FIELD_FRAMES=none on all 30 width-200 entries (E0074, E0075, E0076). The two-line change in field_recorder.py handles the none value. The claim that no analysis tool reads the stored height grids is verified: loop_analysis.py reads only 'spec' and 'L' from fields.npz; pattern_id.py computes its own field from checkpoint.npz particle positions. No departures.

run_conditions.assessment: The session ran from 00:08 to 00:20 on Nov 21 (12 minutes), well within its limit. No simulations were run (the work was a configuration change and collecting a finished job), so zero CPU-hours is correct. No sleep or wake events appear in the pmset log for the session window. Free disk was 17 GB at the start and end, matching the summary. The queue correctly holds the width-200 passes while disk is below the 25.5 GB launch floor.
discrepancies: The session reports disk_gb spent as 9.7 (from du -sh on sequel-data), while program check counts 4.4 from the ledger.
